candidate.answerReason: Writing the reversed numbers by their digits gives m²=99(a-b)(a+b). Prime divisibility forces a+b=11, and square and parity restrictions force a-b=1. Thus x=65, y=56, m=33, and their sum is 154.

methods.label: Use the digit sum and digit difference
methods.explanation:
Reversing digits makes the sum and difference of the numbers easy to factor. Write
\[
x=10a+b,\qquad y=10b+a.
\]
Both numbers are two-digit integers, so \(a,b\) are digits from \(1\) through \(9\). Also, \(m>0\) implies \(x>y\), hence \(a>b\). Factoring the difference of squares gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
m^2&=(x-y)(x+y)\\
&=9(a-b)\cdot11(a+b)\\
&=99(a-b)(a+b).
\end{aligned}
\]
Because the primes \(3\) and \(11\) divide \(m^2\), they both divide \(m\). Thus \(m=33t\) for a positive integer \(t\). Substitution and cancellation give
\[
(a-b)(a+b)=11t^2.
\]
The prime \(11\) must divide one of \(a-b\) and \(a+b\). But \(1\le a-b\le8\), so it cannot divide \(a-b\). Since \(3\le a+b\le17\), the only possibility is
\[
a+b=11.
\]
The previous equation now gives \(a-b=t^2\). As \(1\le t^2\le8\), we have \(t=1\) or \(t=2\). Moreover, \(a-b=11-2b\) is odd, excluding \(t=2\). Thus \(a-b=1\), which together with \(a+b=11\) gives \(a=6\) and \(b=5\).

Therefore \(x=65\), \(y=56\), and \(m=33\). These values satisfy \(65^2-56^2=33^2\), and the restrictions above exclude every other digit pair. Hence
\[
x+y+m=65+56+33=\boxed{154},
\]
choice E.
